methods.name: Set
methods.description:
Save the organization's key for a provider.

 Allowed on every plan. The key is checked once against the provider
 (or the base URL, when one is given) before it is saved, and a key the
 provider rejects is refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT, as is a base URL
 that is not https or does not resolve to a public address. Returns the
 saved key without its secret.

methods.name: Delete
methods.description:
Remove the organization's key for a provider.

 NOT_FOUND when the organization holds no key for
 the provider. Returns the removed key without its secret.

methods.name: List
methods.description:
List the keys that serve the organization, its own and any it inherits
 from its parent organization, without their secrets.

methodTypes.name: SetProviderKeyInput
methodTypes.description:
Save the organization's key for a provider, replacing any key it holds for
 that provider.

fields.name: ApiKey
fields.description: The provider API key. Write-only: no read returns it.

fields.name: BaseUrl
fields.description:
The endpoint to use the key against, as the provider's own SDK takes it
 as its base URL: OpenAI's usually ends in /v1, Anthropic's does not.
 Empty means the provider's own API. Otherwise an absolute https URL
 with no credentials, query or fragment, that resolves to a public
 address; the proxy appends the provider's request path to it, without
 repeating a trailing /v1. For example
 "https://my-resource.openai.azure.com/openai/v1".

methodTypes.name: DeleteProviderKeyInput
methodTypes.description: Remove the organization's key for a provider.

fields.name: PageSize
fields.description:
The most entries to return: 0 asks for the default page of 50, and a
 size above 100 is read as 100.

fields.name: PageToken
fields.description:
The previous response's next_page_token, to continue that list; every
 other field must equal that request's, or the call is refused.

fields.name: Entries
fields.description:
One row per provider the organization is served on its own or its
 parent organization's key, in provider order.

fields.name: NextPageToken
fields.description:
Set when more entries may follow: pass it as page_token to continue.
 A page may be short, even empty, and still carry a token.

enumTypes.name: ProviderKeyCheck
enumTypes.description:
The outcome of the check a save makes with the provider.

 A save asks the provider once whether it accepts the key. A refusal (the
 provider's 401 or 403) refuses the save; any other answer, or none,
 saves the key unchecked, and its first run says whether it works.

values.name: unchecked
values.description:
The provider could not be asked or did not answer plainly; the key was
 saved without its confirmation.

resourceDescription:
An organization's own model provider key, as every caller sees it: the key
 itself never leaves the server, only which provider it is for, a hint to
 tell two keys apart, and who saved it and when.

 An organization holds at most one key per provider, where the provider
 names the wire protocol: "anthropic" is Anthropic's API or any endpoint
 that speaks it, and "openai" is OpenAI's API or any endpoint that speaks
 it.

 The Stigmer Cloud proxy serves every one of the organization's calls to
 that provider on this key, on every plan, and on no other: a run that
 needs a provider the organization holds no key for (by its model) is
 refused with FAILED_PRECONDITION, reason PROVIDER_KEY_REQUIRED, and
 PlatformQueryController.getModelReadiness says so before a run is tried.
 The provider bills the organization directly, and Stigmer meters the calls
 without charging them.

 Provider keys are not an API resource. They are keyed by organization and
 provider, and they authorize against the organization, as billing does.
